panel.summary: The promote gate accepts any `agent-review-*` check run without verifying the producing App, so a token with checks:write can forge panel approval
panel.evidence: `checkPassed` (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:7) filters check runs by `r.name` only. mark-ready.mjs:135-146 feeds it the raw `/commits/{sha}/check-runs` list and its comment claims "the author agent cannot forge them". The review-panel's own guard does verify provenance — agent-review-panel.yml:334 and :358 both require `r.app.slug === 'github-actions'` precisely so "a stray same-prefixed check from some other installed app can't inflate the counter" — so the gate script is the weaker, unguarded entry point to the same evidence. Any actor with checks:write can POST a check run named `agent-review-security` / `agent-review-correctness` with conclusion `success` on the PR head SHA and satisfy gate 2, promoting a PR the panel blocked. The reachable holder of such a token is the unscoped App token in agent-iterate-ci.yml:59 (see the least-privilege finding), which is handed to a Bash-enabled, injection-reachable agent that this diff brings to life. Blast radius is bounded by main's required human approval (agent-implement.yml:116-118), which is why this is major rather than critical.
panel.finding_key: scripts/agent/checks.mjs::the promote gate accepts any `agent-review-*` check run without verifying the producing app, so a token with checks:write can forge panel approval
